title: 4/22-23 systemd watchdog SIGABRT killed the sleeping scheduler every ~30.5 min overnight (NRestarts=21)
tier_reason: liveness failure: a kill/restart loop of the production scheduler (21 automatic restarts overnight)

contract.text: Under Type=notify with WatchdogSec=1800, every scheduler wait longer than the watchdog interval sends sd_notify WATCHDOG pings, so a healthy sleeping daemon is never killed.
contract.source: ARCHITECTURE.md at 4bd8193 (bts-scheduler.service Type=notify, WatchdogSec=1800; 'Heartbeat-watchdog discipline: any time.sleep(>60s) must be wrapped')

mechanism.text: three SLEEPING-state waits in run_day (main-loop sleep between checks, fallback-deadline wait, pre-result-polling wait) were bare time.sleep calls with no notify_watchdog; once the box unit ran with WatchdogSec=1800 (Phase B, 4/22), systemd SIGABRT-ed the daemon about 30 min into each long sleep and Restart=always relaunched it into the same sleep

verified_recovered.how: ddee3db body: NRestarts stayed 0 from the 684c160 deploy restart until both games ended, and the later restarts were clean exits, 'not SIGABRT'

residual.text: The doubleheader game-2 recheck loop kept two un-pinged 15-min sleeps (enough to trip WatchdogSec=1800) after this fix; found by the Fable-5 audit (#6) and closed by ce5f51d (6/09).
residual.source: docs/audit/2026-06-09-fable5-full-audit.md (DH game-2 recheck); src/bts/scheduler.py at c43869d line ~975; ce5f51d

watchdog.trigger: three or more unplanned scheduler restarts within 60 minutes (NRestarts delta or journal lifecycle lines), or any watchdog/SIGABRT exit of bts-scheduler
watchdog.recovery_assertion: NRestarts unchanged across a full overnight sleep and the next day's first scheduled check runs

evidence.what: observed live overnight 4/22-23: NRestarts=21 since the deploy of c43869d at 16:30 the previous day; every ~30:30 min (matching WatchdogSec) the scheduler was killed while in idle-end-of-day / next-wake sleep
on 4/23 NRestarts grew from 0 only after both games ended, and those restarts were 'clean process exits, not SIGABRT'

deploy of c43869d created 2026-04-22T20:30:30Z (16:30:30 ET), the restart from which the NRestarts count in ev1 runs
the box unit became Type=notify + WatchdogSec=1800 + NotifyAccess=all + RestartSec=30 in Phase B (was Type=simple, RestartSec=300); the unit files were box-only until cca6761 (7/10)

notes: config + code interaction: the WatchdogSec=1800 unit was a hand edit on the box on 4/22 (no repo ref); the code defect is the un-pinged sleeps

onset bound is the counting baseline in ev1 (restart at the c43869d deploy); kills may also have occurred between the Phase B unit change and 16:30 (not evidenced); by arithmetic 21 kills at ~30.5 min imply the first counted kill no later than about 00:15 ET 4/23
alert unknown: whether the restarts reached the operator through Healthchecks (heartbeat monitor) is not recorded; the operator found NRestarts=21 by inspection
